findings.quote: A donation from a private organization may fall within the exception when it is considered and accepted as humanitarian or altruistic in purpose and mission.
findings.problem: Humanitarian and altruistic determine whether the exception applies, but neither is explained in simple words. Several named outside roles, including trustee and nominee, are also undefined. No supplied prerequisite teaches these terms.

findings.quote: Do not add the separate "no office transaction" condition from the nominal-donation exception unless the facts of the item require that different exception.
findings.problem: The humanitarian exception is named and distinguished from another exception, but its own meaning is not taught. Neither this paragraph nor example #12 explains what makes a donation humanitarian or altruistic, so students cannot classify a concrete donation by that criterion.

checked: Outside employment states express statutory permission. Private practice requires legal permission plus no conflict and has a distinct former-office one-year limit. Recommendation continuation is expressly one year. Gift teaching distinguishes unsolicited/no favor, family/no financial benefit, nominal donor/no transactions, separate humanitarian purpose, government entities, nominal foreign courtesy, foreign study/treatment, and foreign travel location/interests/head permission.
All three flagged uses of mark occur in mark of courtesy, meaning a sign of courtesy. None describes a score. No cards or score marks occur.
